title: POC Weekly Sync - SDK Tool/Function Calls + Structured Output
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's integration progress: SDK usage for tool/function calls, structured output formatting, early latency and correctness numbers, and outstanding security items. Agreed actions: Marcus to run end-to-end benchmark, Priya to validate schema with frontend, Lena to share updated SDK snippet and pricing; follow-up on May 20.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-13 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Priya, Samir, Elena

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 40 minutes. quick agenda: integration updates, review test results, structured output issues, and security questions.
[00:18] Priya: sounds good, we have 30 minutes blocked for the demo part, but go ahead.
[00:28] Marcus: quick note, we pushed the SDK snippet to your repo branch, it's under /integrations/redwood-poc, the function calling example is included. there was one mismatch in the schema so we added a validation helper.
[00:44] Samir: yep we saw that, small thing: the SDK example uses function_name: "fulfill_order" but our tool is called order_fulfiller, so we adjusted locally. transcription maybe says order filler, not fulfiller.
[01:05] Elena: also the structured output — sometimes the amount field comes back as string, frontend expects number, that's causing a small error.
[01:20] Marcus: right, we observed that when the model returns JSON it's loosely typed; the SDK helper enforces cast rules, and we added a strict JSON schema check option you can toggle.
[01:37] Priya: can you walk us through the flow one more time? from API call to tool invocation to the backend event.
[01:45] Marcus: sure. high level: app calls Redwood SDK -> SDK issues chat/completion with tool definitions attached -> model decides to call function/tool -> Redwood runtime returns a structured tool call payload (name + args) -> SDK maps to local function and calls your service -> your service returns result which SDK normalizes back into the chat context. we added trace_id through headers for debugging.
[02:12] Priya: trace_id is great. is that included in logs visible in Redwood console?
[02:20] Lena: yes, you'll see token-level traces in the Console; for dedicated/private installs those traces are still available but retained according to your retention policy.
[02:28] Samir: on performance — we ran end-to-end tests yesterday. numbers were a bit higher than expected. total latency avg ~420ms for a 200-token call with one tool invocation. is that in line with what you expect on hosted?
[02:45] Marcus: 420ms end-to-end sounds reasonable given your region and the extra hop to your tool. for hosted we typically see model response ~120-180ms for that model and token length, then SDK + network adds the rest. did you run with batching enabled?
[03:05] Samir: no batching, single request per user event. we can try batch inference for background tasks.
[03:12] Marcus: ok batching will help throughput but not p99 for sync calls. also KV cache may shave a chunk if you have repeated prefixes. are you using caching?
[03:22] Priya: we haven't integrated KV cache yet. is that automatic or SDK-level?
[03:27] Marcus: it's runtime-level; you need to opt-in via config in the SDK: enable_prefix_cache: true and set cache_ttl. note when using private deployment you'll have to configure a Redis endpoint or use the local cache option.
[03:44] Elena: related to that, for PCI-sensitive flows we need to keep everything on-prem. what's the path for private deployment?
[03:52] Lena: Private deployment options include VPC or full on-prem package. for POC we can spin a VPC private control plane; for full on-prem we'll do an infra workshop. I'll connect you to Solutions for that.
[04:10] Samir: great. any SOC2/ISO docs?
[04:14] Lena: yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO27001, plus a DR plan excerpt. I'll attach those to the workspace.
[04:22] Elena: back to structured output — we saw a case where model emitted trailing commas in JSON and parser failed, also sometimes added commentary outside the JSON block.
[04:34] Marcus: that happens; we recommend function-calling where the model returns a clean tool payload rather than freeform. if you must parse freeform, use the sdk's resilient_json_parser which attempts to recover. but best is to define a strict json schema in the function signature so model is constrained.
[04:56] Priya: how do we define that schema? example?
[05:00] Marcus: here's an example snippet (we pasted to the repo):
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "order_fulfiller",
      "description": "Trigger order fulfillment",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "order_id": {"type": "string"},
          "amount": {"type": "number"},
          "items": {"type": "array"}
        },
        "required": ["order_id","amount"]
      }
    }
  ]
Marcus: when the model responds it will return a JSON block matching that. SDK's validate_and_cast will coerce types where possible or raise.
[06:10] Priya: are there any quota considerations for function-calls? we expect a lot of short calls.
[06:18] Lena: function calls count as a standard chat completion request; cost is per token returned plus a small fixed per-request surcharge in some pricing tiers. we'll send the updated pricing sheet.
[06:32] Samir: about fallbacks — if the primary model fails, can we route to a cheaper/safer model automatically?
[06:38] Marcus: yes, Redwood supports routing policies: latency-first or cost-first fallbacks; you can configure a chain: primary_model -> quantized variant -> small LLM. the SDK includes an on_failure hook.
[06:58] Elena: earlier you mentioned KV cache and quantization for cost. any gotchas when combined with function calls?
[07:06] Marcus: quantization affects model quality a bit more for structured outputs; if your schema is tight, lower-bit models may hallucinate slightly more. so for mission-critical structured outputs, we recommend at least 4-bit quant or binarized checks. also caching doesn't change the semantics of function calls, but prefix caching only helps when the prompt prefix is similar.
[07:30] Priya: ok. about testing: Marcus, can you re-run the end-to-end with the SDK instrumented to include timing breakdowns? we want tokenization, model time, network, and our service time.
[07:43] Marcus: yes, I'll run a benchmark harness. I'll include p50/p90/p99 and a CSV. expected to complete by next Tuesday.
[07:53] Priya: next Tuesday is May 20, that works.
[07:58] Lena: putting that as action item.
[08:02] Samir: we also need an example of error handling patterns for the frontend when structured output validation fails. any recommended approach?
[08:10] Marcus: best practice: SDK returns a normalized object or raises ValidationError with details, we suggest showing a friendly fallback on frontend and queue a retry for async flows. we added sample code in /examples/error-handling.js.
[08:28] Elena: perfect. my team will validate the schema with our product mapper and get back if adjustments needed.
[08:35] Priya: another question — does the SDK support streaming for function calls? like partial tool args as the model generates?
[08:44] Marcus: we have streaming for token outputs; function/tool call is typically atomic: you receive the function payload once model decides to call. partial streaming of structured payloads isn't generally recommended.
[08:58] Lena: does that impact UX for large payloads?
[09:02] Marcus: for large payloads we recommend asynchronous patterns: model returns a small pointer id and you fetch the full payload from a storage endpoint.
[09:12] Priya: ok. security quick check — how is KMS integrated in hosted vs private?
[09:18] Lena: hosted supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for encryption at rest of model artifacts and logs; for private/on-prem you use your own HSM or local KMS endpoint. we'll share architecture diagrams.
[09:33] Samir: please include how audit logs are stored and retention.
[09:36] Lena: noted, will include retention examples.
[09:40] Elena: small bug report: webhook callbacks from our order_fulfiller sometimes drop headers when proxied through our gateway; it's unrelated to Redwood but affects end-to-end tests. we suspect our gateway strips trace headers.
[09:54] Marcus: we can include a test harness which echoes headers to help you debug. I'll add that to the repo.
[10:02] Priya: regarding observability, we want per-route latency breakdowns, can Redwood Console do that?
[10:08] Lena: yes, per-route, per-model token breakdowns are available; we can create a custom dashboard for your routes.
[10:16] Samir: any data residency options for EU? we have a footprint there.
[10:20] Lena: hosted has EU regions, private deployments can be provisioned in-region; we'll document region-specific SLAs.
[10:28] Elena: demo time — Samir, you said you ran tests, can you show one trace?
[10:33] Samir: yes sharing screen, here's a single request trace. [screen pause] I see model time 160ms, network out 70ms, our order service 200ms, total ~430ms. you can see sdk trace_id: trace-9921.
[11:05] Marcus: that matches expectation; we can try bringing service time down or run model in-region.
[11:12] Priya: if we move the model closer, is there cost change?
[11:16] Marcus: region egress and instance types can change price a bit; we'll include an expected delta in the cost sheet.
[11:24] Lena: ok, let's capture open items.
[11:28] Marcus: action item: run end-to-end benchmark with timing breakdowns and p99 by May 20.
[11:36] Priya: action: validate structured schema with frontend and post results by May 18.
[11:42] Samir: action: check gateway trace header passthrough and report by May 17.
[11:49] Lena: action: share SOC2/ISO docs, updated pricing, and the SDK snippet with the strict schema example by EOD today.
[12:00] Elena: one more thing — for our POC success criteria we need: <1s median latency, <500ms model time, structured output pass rate >99% on validation, and docs/pricing for private deploy.
[12:18] Marcus: noted, we'll prioritize reproducible tests for those metrics.
[12:24] Lena: any final questions?
[12:28] Priya: none from me, thanks.
[12:30] Elena: all good.
[12:33] Samir: good meeting.
[12:36] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the next call scheduled May 20 for benchmark review.

End of transcript.
